meanings.note: Feminine: actrice. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'actor'.

meanings.note: Trois cents, but trois cent mille. Spoken French num expression meaning 'hundred', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: Une couleur plus claire. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'clear'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je ne saute pas sur le canard, c'est clair?

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.trans: The water is lovely, you can try.

examples.trans: No, thank you. A glass of water.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

Clothes. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to try'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'essayé').

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced. French conjunction meaning 'and', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'exciting'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

meanings.note: Une fois, deux fois = once, twice. Feminine noun ('la fois', plural 'les fois') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'time'.

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two. I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: Goes before the noun. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'young'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

meanings.note: Adverb: je veux juste. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
